```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2) })
PARENT <- "/project/spott/cshan/fiber-seq/code/clustering_methods/auto_correlation"
PYTHON <- "/project/spott/cshan/envs/Jupyter-notebook/bin/python"
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("RETICULATE_PYTHON"))) Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = PYTHON)
library(reticulate)

# parent functions, unchanged: summarize() from 05_summarize_autocorrelations.py, the
# report functions of 06_autocorrelation.Rmd, and the shared plotting helpers
source("/project/spott/cshan/fiber-seq/code/parsing_functions/plotting_functions.r")
source_python(file.path(PARENT, "05_summarize_autocorrelations.py"))
eval(parse(text = import_from_path("01_run_autocorrelation", path = PARENT)$report_function_code()))

out  <- params$out_dir
figs <- file.path(out, "figures")
dir.create(figs, showWarnings = FALSE)
lags <- params$lag_from:params$lag_to
```

```{r data}
res <- readRDS(file.path(out, "outputs", "acf_all_genes.rds"))$genes
ok  <- vapply(res, function(r) is.null(r$error), logical(1))
genes <- rbindlist(lapply(res[ok], `[[`, "gene"))
n_run <- nrow(genes)
genes <- genes[n_acf_valid >= params$min_reads]
genes[, `:=`(log10_pi = log10(pi), log10_tpm = log10(mean_tpm))]
setorder(genes, log10_pi)
# equal-count fifths of log10 PI; C1 = lowest PI, C5 = highest
genes[, pi_quintile := cut(log10_pi, quantile(log10_pi, 0:5 / 5), include.lowest = TRUE,
                           labels = FALSE)]
quintiles  <- paste0("C", 1:5)
pi_colours <- cluster_id_palette(quintiles)

# one row per gene in PI order: per-gene mean ACF (lag 0-1999) and mean m6A per TSS offset
acf_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genes$region_id, function(g) res[[g]]$curves$mean_acf))
m6a_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genes$region_id, function(g) res[[g]]$m6a_profile$mean_m6a))
offsets <- res[[genes$region_id[1]]]$m6a_profile$offset_bp
stopifnot(!anyNA(acf_mat), ncol(acf_mat) > params$lag_to, !anyNA(m6a_mat),
          all(vapply(genes$region_id, function(g)
            identical(res[[g]]$m6a_profile$offset_bp, offsets), logical(1))))
rm(res)
```

# Question

Does nucleosome phasing at the TSS change with RNA Pol II pausing, when pausing is
treated as a continuous variable across every eligible gene rather than as six matched
high/low pairs (`tss_autocorrelation.Rmd`)?

# Data

Stage 04 selected `r format(n_run, big.mark = ",")` isolated, expressed protein-coding
TSSs, and stage 05 computed the per-read m6A autocorrelation for each one in a
[-1000, +1000) bp window oriented in the direction of transcription, pooling reads from
the 31 LCL samples. Genes with fewer than `r params$min_reads` ACF-valid reads are
dropped here, the same filter as the stage 06 regression, which leaves
**`r format(nrow(genes), big.mark = ",")` genes**.

For display, genes are cut into five equal-sized groups by log10 PI, C1 (lowest) to C5
(highest). The regression in stage 06 does not use these groups; it uses log10 PI as a
continuous predictor. The labels are C1-C5 because the curve figure is drawn with the
parent pipeline's cluster function, unchanged, with the PI quintile in place of the
Leiden cluster.

```{r quintile-table}
genes[, .(genes = .N, pi_min = signif(min(pi), 3), pi_median = signif(median(pi), 3),
          pi_max = signif(max(pi), 3), tpm_median = round(median(mean_tpm), 1),
          reads_median = as.numeric(median(n_acf_valid)),
          m6a_fraction_median = round(median(mean_m6a_call_fraction), 4)),
      by = .(quintile = paste0("C", pi_quintile))][order(quintile)]
```

# The regression (stage 06)

`outcome ~ log10(PI) + log10(TPM)`, one row per gene, over the genes with a peak in
140-250 bp. Expression is the only covariate; it replaces the pilot's matching on
expression.

```{r regression}
fit <- fread(file.path(out, "tables", "pi_regression.tsv"))
fit[, .(outcome, term, estimate = signif(estimate, 3), conf_low = signif(conf_low, 3),
        conf_high = signif(conf_high, 3), p_value = signif(p_value, 3), n_genes,
        r_squared = signif(r_squared, 3))]
```

# Figures

All figures are written as PDFs to ``r figs``.

## 1. Mean ACF by PI quintile

Each gene's mean ACF counts once (genes weighted equally, not molecules), averaged within
each quintile by the parent `summarize()` and drawn by the parent
`plot_report_cluster_acf()`. In the legend, n is the number of genes. The peak marked
in the table below is `repeat_peak()` applied to each quintile's mean curve.

```{r fig-quintile-acf, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
records <- data.frame(region_id = "all_tss", RID = genes$region_id, sample_name = "all",
                      m6a_call_fraction = genes$mean_m6a_call_fraction,
                      cluster = genes$pi_quintile, status = "clustered")
s <- summarize(acf_mat, records)
quintile_acf   <- as.data.table(s[[1]])
quintile_peaks <- as.data.table(s[[2]])
region_data <- list(
  region = list(region_id = sprintf("%s isolated protein-coding TSSs",
                                    format(nrow(genes), big.mark = ",")),
                focal_snp = "log10 PI quintiles", ref = "C1 lowest", alt = "C5 highest"),
  tables = list(cluster_acf_summary = as.data.frame(quintile_acf)))
p <- plot_report_cluster_acf(region_data, lower = params$lag_from, upper = params$lag_to,
                             title = "Mean ACF per PI quintile, genes weighted equally; no smoothing")
save_figure(p, file.path(figs, "01_pi_quintile_mean_acf.pdf"), width = 9, height = 7)
p
```

```{r quintile-peaks}
quintile_peaks[, .(quintile = paste0("C", cluster), genes = n_reads,
                   peak_lag_bp = positive_local_peak_140_250_bp,
                   peak_acf = signif(peak_acf, 3))]
```

The quintile curves peak lower than single genes do, because each gene peaks at a
different lag and averaging spreads the peaks out.

## 2. Per-gene peak height and lag vs pausing index

One point per gene, coloured by its m6A call fraction. The line is the stage 06 fit for
log10 PI, drawn at the median log10 TPM of the plotted genes.

```{r fig-peak-vs-pi, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.5}
peak_panel <- function(y, ylab) {
  co <- fit[outcome == y]
  b  <- setNames(co$estimate, co$term)
  d  <- genes[is.finite(get(y))]
  stopifnot(co$n_genes[1] == nrow(d))   # the same genes as stage 06
  slope <- co[term == "log10_pi"]
  ggplot(d, aes(log10_pi, .data[[y]], colour = mean_m6a_call_fraction)) +
    geom_point(size = .5, alpha = .6) +
    geom_abline(intercept = b[["(Intercept)"]] + b[["log10_tpm"]] * median(d$log10_tpm),
                slope = b[["log10_pi"]], colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = .8) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "m6A call\nfraction") +
    labs(x = "log10 pausing index", y = ylab,
         subtitle = sprintf("log10 PI slope %.3g (95%% CI %.3g to %.3g), p = %.2g, n = %d",
                            slope$estimate, slope$conf_low, slope$conf_high,
                            slope$p_value, slope$n_genes)) +
    theme_fiberseq("bw")
}
p <- cowplot::plot_grid(peak_panel("peak_height", "ACF peak height (140-250 bp)"),
                        peak_panel("peak_lag_bp", "ACF peak lag (bp)"), ncol = 2)
save_figure(p, file.path(figs, "02_peak_vs_pi.pdf"), width = 11, height = 4.5)
p
```

## 3. Every gene's mean ACF, ordered by pausing index

One row per gene, lowest PI at the bottom; dashed lines separate the quintiles. Colour
saturates at the 99th percentile of |ACF| over the lags shown.

```{r fig-gene-heatmap, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
hm  <- acf_mat[, lags + 1L]
lim <- quantile(abs(hm), .99)
d <- data.table(gene_rank = rep(seq_len(nrow(hm)), times = length(lags)),
                lag_bp = rep(lags, each = nrow(hm)),
                acf = pmax(pmin(as.vector(hm), lim), -lim))
bounds <- genes[, .(top = max(.I)), by = pi_quintile][order(pi_quintile)]
mids   <- genes[, .(mid = mean(.I)), by = pi_quintile][order(pi_quintile)]
p <- ggplot(d, aes(lag_bp, gene_rank, fill = acf)) +
  geom_raster() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = head(bounds$top, -1) + .5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0,
                       limits = c(-lim, lim), name = "Mean ACF") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = mids$mid, labels = quintiles) +
  labs(x = "Lag (bp)", y = "Genes ordered by pausing index (PI quintile)",
       title = sprintf("Per-gene mean ACF, %s genes", format(nrow(genes), big.mark = ",")),
       subtitle = sprintf("colour saturates at the 99th percentile of |ACF| (%.3f)", lim)) +
  theme_fiberseq("bw")
save_figure(p, file.path(figs, "03_gene_acf_heatmap.pdf"), width = 8, height = 9)
p
```

## 4. m6A around the TSS by PI quintile

Mean m6A call fraction at each position, averaged over the genes in each quintile
(genes weighted equally), in the direction of transcription. No smoothing.

```{r fig-tss-m6a, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
prof <- rbindlist(lapply(1:5, function(q)
  data.table(quintile = quintiles[q], offset_bp = offsets,
             mean_m6a = colMeans(m6a_mat[genes$pi_quintile == q, , drop = FALSE]))))
prof[, quintile := factor(quintile, levels = quintiles)]
p <- plot_group_profile(prof, group_col = "quintile", x_col = "offset_bp", y_col = "mean_m6a",
                        colors = pi_colours,
                        markers = list(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50"),
                        labels = list(x = "Position relative to TSS (bp, direction of transcription)",
                                      y = "Mean m6A call fraction", colour = "PI quintile",
                                      title = "m6A at the TSS by PI quintile"),
                        theme = theme_fiberseq("bw"))
save_figure(p, file.path(figs, "04_tss_m6a_by_pi_quintile.pdf"), width = 9, height = 4.5)
p
```
